# Story 08 — Reports show the reader's day in their own zone (Story: CRM-131)

## Prerequisites

- **REPORTS-4-API (CRM-130)** completed: `GET /re
ports/{queue-by-status,promise-share,agent-load}` accept `?timeZone=` (an IANA zone) and optional `?from=YYYY-MM-D
D&to=YYYY-MM-DD`, and each response now carries a **`window`** block (start / end / time
Zone). The API refuses an unknown zone with `422` and `fields: ['timeZone']` — verified in `api/src

/features/reports/reader-day.test.js` (see lines 58–137, 152–191).
- **REPORTS

-1-API (CRM-124)** completed: the three reports endpoints exist and are admin-only.
- Screens today live in `web/src/pages/reports/` (`AgentLoadPage.
tsx`, `PromiseSharePage.tsx`, `QueueByStatusPage.tsx`) and their hooks (`useAgentLoad.ts`, `usePromiseShare.ts`, `useQueueByStatus.ts`
). Their route is registered admin-only in `web/src/app/routes.tsx` alongside `/audit` (see `routes.tsx:161`); this story does **not** touch routing

.

---

## Story Goal

An admin who opens any of the three reports sees numbers stamped with the period they cover, in **their** loc
ale, computed against **their** browser's IANA zone (not UTC, not a language guess). When the reader picks a different preset period,
the request is re-sent with the same zone, the previous numbers are cleared before the new ones land, and the sentence describing the period changes together

with the numbers — never one under the label of the other.

Out of scope (do **not** implement):
- No zone pic

ker (the browser owns the zone).
- No client-side day-boundary math (the client sends the zone; the API decides the rows).
- No calendar wid

get, no date library, no free-form date range input.
- No API changes.

---

## Product rules (from story)

- **BR-3 — Time is UTC in storage,

the reader's locale on display.** Dates rendered on report screens go through `useFormatters().formatDate`.
- **L-51 — Sentences with slots use `
Isolated` (U+2068 / U+2069).** The period sentence is built the way `web/src/pages/tickets/history-sentence.ts` and `web/src/pages/tickets/

pager-sentence.ts` build theirs.
- **L-63 — Don't fire a request the caller knows will be refused.** Existing `enabled` gu

ard is kept.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **`Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().

timeZone` returns empty string.** Fallback is `'UTC'`. Enforced in `reader-zone.ts` (see § 1).
- **API returns `422 { fields: ['timeZone'] }` because the runtime named
a zone the server does not know.** The existing `ErrorState` branch renders `t.errors.UNPROCESSABLE`; no special case. `read

erZone`'s `'UTC'` fallback covers the "no zone at all" path.
- **Reader picks `last7`, then quickly picks `last
30` before the first request lands.** `useRequest` fires the second request; the stale-guard (§ 4) clears the returned `report` on period change, so the scre

en shows the skeleton, not the `last7` numbers under a `last30` label.
- **Language switch mid-page.** The period sentence re-renders from `t` and

the `formatDate` output changes locale; the underlying request is unchanged (locale is not zone).
- **DST boundary during the reader's session
.** `readerZone` is memoised per mount, so a session that crosses DST keeps the same zone id; behaviour matches the API's day-boundary math

(which uses the zone id, not the offset). Documented in a comment beside `useMemo` in each page.
- **Non-admin arrives at the route.** `isAdmin

=== false` still returns the `EmptyState`; the hook is `enabled: false`, so no request is made (L-63).
- **Zone id contains RTL-neutral characters** (`
Africa/Cairo`, `America/New_York`). The zone is rendered inside `<Isolated>` so bidi wrapping keeps it intact in Arabic lay

out.
